findings.desc: typed process fact contract still hard-checks only a subset of artifact facts. Docs/AGENTS say gate/reviewer/artifact drift must be mechanically covered, but verify-process-fact-contract only enforces requiredArtifactFacts and omits some gate-consumed artifacts such as review.json plus artifact refs hanging off commands like summary_set/verify_codex. This leaves a concept gap between documented contract scope and actual hard enforcement.

scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs still trusts compiled dist modules before source. parseProcessFactRegistry() reads packages/main/dist/core/process-fact-registry.js when it exists, and the same verifier also imports built command-policy/config modules, so npm run test:process-fact-contract can validate stale build output instead of the current src edits. This makes contract diagnostics non-deterministic for maintainers unless they rebuild first, which violates the goal of stable drift detection. Fix by making the verifier source-first for contract checks, or by rejecting stale dist via explicit freshness/hash checks before using compiled modules.

verify-process-fact-contract.mjs still does not provide stable source-of-truth diagnostics for the new registry. First, parseProcessFactRegistry() and the surrounding helpers trust compiled dist modules before current source, so npm run test:process-fact-contract can validate stale build output instead of current src edits unless maintainers rebuild first. Second, the source fallback path only token-checks process-fact-registry.ts and then reconstructs entries from helper exports instead of validating the final exported PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY composition, so export-level drift like dropping PROCESS_FACT_ARTIFACTS or PROCESS_FACT_REVIEWER_LANES can evade fallback checks. Fix by making contract verification source-first (or rejecting stale dist with explicit freshness/hash checks) and by parsing/asserting the final PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY export rather than synthesizing it from helpers in fallback mode.

verify-process-fact-contract is source-first now, but its source parser still synthesizes registry entries instead of validating the final exported registry shapes. parseProcessFactRegistry() rebuilds command facts from PROCESS_FACT_LEVELS plus COMMAND_POLICIES and hard-codes reviewer-lane kind/semantics/level from PROCESS_FACT_REVIEWER_LANE_DEFINITIONS, while only token-checking the final PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY spread list. Because the verifier always runs in this fallback path, drift inside COMMAND_PROCESS_FACTS or PROCESS_FACT_REVIEWER_LANES/exported mapping logic can still pass without being checked against the actual exported PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY objects. Make the verifier parse/assert the exported COMMAND_PROCESS_FACTS / PROCESS_FACT_REVIEWER_LANES / final PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY values, or compare source-derived output against the built export with an explicit freshness guard.
